title: Config
description:
Main configuration struct.

## Hot-reload behaviour

The config file is watched for changes. When reloaded, values are
available via `SharedConfig::get()`. However, not all settings take
effect without a restart.

**Hot-reloaded (takes effect on next fetch cycle):**
- `scheduler.default_interval_secs` — fetch interval re-computed each cycle
- `scheduler.jitter_percent` — jitter re-computed each cycle
- `kafka.topic_suffix` — topic name suffix re-read on each delivery
- `sources.*.filter` — CEL filter re-evaluated on each record
- `cursor.default_window_hours` — lookback window re-read when no cursor exists

**Requires pod restart:**
- `output.*` — transport connections established at startup
- `kafka.*` (except `topic_suffix`) — transport config bound at startup
- `ingest.*` — HTTP server binds at startup, auth token resolved once
- `extractors.*` — containers and Vector instances spawned at startup
- `metrics.*` — metrics server binds at startup
- `instance_id` — cursor key prefix set at startup
- `cursor.directory` — cursor store created at startup
- `sources.*.enabled` — source registration at startup
- `sources.*.credential_secret` / `tenant_id` / `client_id` etc. — credentials resolved once
- `scheduler.max_concurrent_fetches` — semaphore created at startup
- `dlq.*` — DLQ created at startup
- `buffer.*` — buffer manager created at startup

ingest.description: HTTP ingest server configuration (for container extractors to post data).

config_reload_secs.description: Periodic config reload interval in seconds (0 = disabled, SIGHUP only).

instance_id.description:
Instance identity for cursor isolation across multiple fetcher pods.
Auto-derived from source config if omitted.

scaling.description: Scaling pressure configuration for KEDA autoscaling.

unwrap_nested_json.description:
Recursively unwrap double-serialised JSON string fields before delivery.

When enabled (default), any string field whose value parses as a JSON
object or array is replaced with the parsed value. This makes fields
like AWS CloudTrail's `CloudTrailEvent` queryable as nested JSON in
downstream systems like ClickHouse.

Set to `false` for sources that intentionally store JSON as strings.

default_interval_secs.description: Default fetch interval in seconds (used when source doesn't specify its own).

max_concurrent_fetches.description: Maximum concurrent fetch tasks across all sources.

jitter_percent.description: Jitter percentage (0-100) added to intervals to avoid thundering herd.

go_modules.description: Go module-proxy supply-chain audit source configuration.

google_workspace.description:
Google Workspace Reports API source configuration.

**Alpha** - additionally pending hyperi-infra#5 (domain-wide-delegation
service account + manual Admin-console scope grants) before live use.

gcp_pubsub.description:
GCP Pub/Sub pull source configuration.

**Alpha** - additionally pending a hyperi-infra issue (TBD) for
tenant-side Log Sink + Pub/Sub topic + subscription provisioning.

object_store.description:
Object-store source family configuration (S3 / GCS / Azure Blob).

The S3 backend is live; GCS and Azure Blob are stubs that log-and-skip,
so naming them here does not fail the tick.

salesforce.description:
Salesforce audit source configuration (SetupAuditTrail,
LoginHistory, EventLogFile).

**Alpha** - additionally pending a Salesforce connected app for live
testing.

GithubSourceConfig.description:
GitHub source configuration.

Pulls audit-log events from either a GitHub organisation
(`/orgs/{org}/audit-log`) or a GitHub Enterprise Cloud account
(`/enterprises/{enterprise}/audit-log`). Set exactly one of `org` or
`enterprise` per fetcher instance - scale to multiple by deploying multiple
fetcher instances with different configs (per the no-horizontal-scaling rule
in CLAUDE.md).

org.description:
Organisation slug for `/orgs/{org}/audit-log`. Exactly one of `org` /
`enterprise` must be set when enabled.

enterprise.description:
Enterprise slug for `/enterprises/{enterprise}/audit-log`. Requires a
GitHub Enterprise Cloud plan.

token.description:
Personal Access Token, fine-grained PAT, or GitHub App installation
token. Required scope: `read:audit_log` (org) or `read:enterprise`
(enterprise). Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token (e.g. `vault:secret/github:token`).

api_url_override.description: API base URL override for testing (e.g. wiremock).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple orgs/enterprises of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

GithubService.description: GitHub service to fetch data from.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for `audit_log`:
- `include`: one of `"all"` (default), `"web"`, or `"git"`.

GithubConnection.description:
One GitHub connection: an org or enterprise + its token. Type-wide fields
(`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`GithubSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token ("provider:path:key").

api_url_override.description: API base URL override for testing.

OktaSourceConfig.description:
Okta source configuration.

Pulls events from the Okta System Log API
(`{tenant_url}/api/v1/logs`). One Okta tenant per fetcher instance.

tenant_url.description:
Tenant URL, e.g. `https://hyperi.okta.com` (no trailing slash).
The OAuth-style preview API uses `oktapreview.com`; either is accepted
here verbatim. Override per environment.

token.description:
SSWS API token (legacy auth) or bearer token from OAuth.
Always redacted on serialisation.

use_ssws_header.description:
If `true`, send the token as `Authorization: SSWS <token>` (Okta's
legacy API-token header). If `false`, send as `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` (OAuth access token). Default: `true`.

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token (e.g. `vault:secret/okta:token`).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple tenants of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

OktaService.description: Okta service to fetch data from.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for `system_log`:
- `filter`: OData-style filter applied server-side
  (e.g. `eventType eq "user.session.start"`).
- `limit`: per-page size (Okta caps at 1000).

OktaConnection.description:
One Okta connection: a tenant URL + its token. Type-wide fields (`services`,
`topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on [`OktaSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

token.description: SSWS API token or OAuth bearer token (always redacted).

use_ssws_header.description:
Override the SSWS vs Bearer header choice for this connection.
Inherits the type-level `use_ssws_header` when unset.

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token ("provider:path:key").

CloudflareSourceConfig.description:
Cloudflare source configuration.

Pulls events from Cloudflare's REST API. One account per fetcher instance.
Auth: scoped API token (read-only). Account ID required for audit logs.

account_id.description: Account ID (32-char hex) for account-level audit logs.

token.description:
API token. Always redacted on serialisation.
Required token permission for the v1 account audit-logs endpoint this
source calls (`/accounts/{id}/audit_logs`): **Account Settings: Read**.
(The separate "Account Audit Logs Read" permission applies to the
newer v2 `/accounts/{id}/logs/audit` API, which this source does not
use yet.)

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token (e.g. `vault:secret/cloudflare:token`).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple accounts of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

CloudflareService.description: Cloudflare service to fetch data from.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for `audit_logs`:
- `actor_email`: filter by acting user (optional).
- `action_type`: filter by action category (optional).
- `per_page`: page size (default 100, max 1000).

CloudflareConnection.description:
One Cloudflare connection: an account + its token. Type-wide fields
(`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`CloudflareSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

account_id.description: Account ID (32-char hex) for account-level audit logs.

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token ("provider:path:key").

OnePasswordSourceConfig.description:
1Password Events Reporting source configuration.

Pulls events from the 1Password Events Reporting API
(`events.1password.com/api/v2/*`). Requires a 1Password Business or
Enterprise account with Events Reporting enabled.

token.description:
Events Reporting API token (Bearer token, generated from the
1Password Business dashboard). Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the token
(e.g. `vault:secret/onepassword:events_token`).

api_url_override.description:
API base override for testing.
Production default: `https://events.1password.com`.
EU-region tenants: `https://events.ent.1password.eu`.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple 1Password accounts of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

OnePasswordService.description:
1Password service to fetch data from. Each maps to one Events Reporting
endpoint: `signinattempts`, `itemusages`, or `auditevents`.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys:
- `limit`: page size (default 100, max 1000).

OnePasswordConnection.description:
One 1Password connection: an account + its Events Reporting token. Type-wide
fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`OnePasswordSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

token.description: Events Reporting API token (always redacted on serialisation).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token ("provider:path:key").

CrowdstrikeSourceConfig.description:
CrowdStrike Falcon source configuration.

Pulls detections, incidents, and host data from CrowdStrike Falcon's
public API via OAuth2 client_credentials. Region-aware: each Falcon
instance lives on a different cloud (US-1, US-2, EU-1, US-GOV-1) and
the API host changes accordingly.

api_url_override.description:
API base URL for the region the tenant lives on.
Examples:
- US-1: `https://api.crowdstrike.com` (default)
- US-2: `https://api.us-2.crowdstrike.com`
- EU-1: `https://api.eu-1.crowdstrike.com`
- US-GOV-1: `https://api.laggar.gcw.crowdstrike.com`

client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID (Falcon API client, created in Falcon admin console).

client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret. Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the client_secret
(e.g. `vault:secret/crowdstrike:client_secret`).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Falcon tenants of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

CrowdstrikeService.description: CrowdStrike service to fetch data from.

name.description:
Service name (currently only "detections" - returns enriched
EPP detection summaries).

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for `detections`:
- `limit`: query page size (default 100, max 9999).
- `filter`: Falcon Query Language clause appended to the auto-built
  `created_timestamp:>'<start>'+created_timestamp:<'<end>'`.

CrowdstrikeConnection.description:
One CrowdStrike connection: a Falcon tenant (region + OAuth2 client). Type-
wide fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`CrowdstrikeSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

api_url_override.description: API base URL for the region the tenant lives on.

client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret (always redacted on serialisation).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the client_secret ("provider:path:key").

SlackSourceConfig.description:
Slack audit-log source configuration.

Pulls audit-log events from `https://api.slack.com/audit/v1/logs`.
Enterprise Grid only - requires an Org Admin token with the
`auditlogs:read` scope.

token.description:
Org-admin user token (xoxa-... or xoxb-...) with `auditlogs:read`.
Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the token
(e.g. `vault:secret/slack:audit_token`).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Slack orgs of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

SlackService.description: Slack service to fetch data from.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for `audit_logs`:
- `action`: filter by action name (e.g. `user_login`).
- `entity`: filter by entity type (`user` / `workspace` / etc).
- `limit`: per-page size (default 200, max 1000).

SlackConnection.description:
One Slack connection: an Enterprise Grid org + its admin token. Type-wide
fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`SlackSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

token.description: Org-admin user token (always redacted on serialisation).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the token ("provider:path:key").

Organisation API client ID. Generated in Bitwarden admin:
Settings > Organization info > "View API Key".
Format is `organization.<uuid>`.

client_secret.description: Organisation API client secret. Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the client_secret
(e.g. `vault:secret/bitwarden:client_secret`).

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Bitwarden organisations of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

BitwardenService.description: Bitwarden service to fetch data from.

config.description: Service-specific configuration. No recognised keys yet.

BitwardenConnection.description:
One Bitwarden connection: an organisation + its API credentials. Type-wide
fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`BitwardenSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

client_secret.description: Organisation API client secret (always redacted on serialisation).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the client_secret ("provider:path:key").

DuoSourceConfig.description:
Duo Admin API source configuration.

Pulls authentication events from a Duo tenant's
`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com/admin/v2/logs/authentication` endpoint.
Auth uses Duo's proprietary scheme: HMAC-SHA1 over a canonical request
signature, transported in a Basic auth header.

api_host.description:
API hostname (without scheme). Format: `api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`.
Available in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Admin API.

integration_key.description: Integration key (`ikey`). Identifies the Admin API integration.

secret_key.description:
Secret key (`skey`). Used to compute the HMAC-SHA1 request signature.
Always redacted on serialisation.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the secret_key
(e.g. `vault:secret/duo:skey`).

api_url_override.description:
API base override for testing (full URL incl. scheme). Production
should use `api_host` only; this is for mock servers.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Duo tenants of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

DuoService.description: Duo service to fetch data from.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys for
`authentication_logs`:
- `limit`: per-page size (default 100, max 1000).

DuoConnection.description:
One Duo connection: a tenant (api_host) + its integration/secret keys.
Type-wide fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`DuoSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the secret_key ("provider:path:key").

PypiSourceConfig.description:
PyPI source configuration.

Fetches metadata for a configured list of PyPI packages on each tick.
Use case: supply-chain monitoring of HyperI-published Python packages -
downstream tooling computes deltas against a known-good baseline and
alerts on unexpected version, file, or maintainer changes.

No authentication required - all responses come from
`https://pypi.org/pypi/<package>/json`.

packages.description: Package names to monitor. Each becomes one record per fetch tick.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

CratesIoSourceConfig.description:
crates.io source configuration.

Fetches metadata for a configured list of crates on each tick.
No authentication required - all responses come from
`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>`.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

GoModulesSourceConfig.description:
Go module-proxy source configuration.

Fetches version list + per-version `.info` metadata for a configured list
of Go modules. The default proxy is Google's at
`https://proxy.golang.org` - free for everyone, GOPROXY-compatible.

No authentication required.

api_url_override.description:
Module proxy base override (default `https://proxy.golang.org`).
Use an internal mirror if desired.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

GoogleWorkspaceSourceConfig.description:
Google Workspace Reports API source configuration.

**Alpha** (code-complete, not production-validated) and additionally
pending hyperi-infra#5. The fetcher code is written
against the documented Workspace Reports API but cannot be live-tested
until the GCP service account is provisioned with domain-wide delegation
and the manual Admin-console scope grants are completed.

Pulls per-application audit/activity reports from
`admin.googleapis.com/admin/reports/v1/activity/users/all/applications/<app>`.
Auth: OAuth2 service account using JWT-with-subject (RS256) - the SA
impersonates a designated Workspace admin email so the Reports API
returns data scoped to the tenant.

service_account_key.description:
Path to the service account JSON key file (same shape as the GCP
source). The SA must have domain-wide delegation enabled and the
required Reports API scopes granted in the Workspace Admin console.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the SA key
(e.g. `vault:secret/google_workspace:sa_key`).

admin_email.description:
Admin email the SA impersonates (the `sub` claim of the signed JWT).
Must be a Workspace admin in the target tenant; without this the
Reports API returns 403.

customer_id.description:
Customer ID. Defaults to `my_customer` (the tenant the SA's
impersonated admin belongs to). Explicit C-prefixed IDs are only
needed for multi-tenant reseller scenarios.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Workspace tenants of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

GoogleWorkspaceService.description:
Google Workspace service. Each maps to one `applicationName` under the
Reports API: `login`, `admin`, `drive`, `mobile`, `groups`, `calendar`,
`chat`, `meet`, `token`, etc.

name.description: Service name; passed directly as the `applicationName` URL segment.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys:
- `event_name`: filter to a single event name (optional).

GoogleWorkspaceConnection.description:
One Google Workspace connection: a tenant (impersonated admin) + its SA key.
Type-wide fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are shared and stay on
[`GoogleWorkspaceSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

service_account_key.description: Path to the service account JSON key file.

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec for the SA key ("provider:path:key").

admin_email.description: Admin email the SA impersonates (the `sub` claim of the signed JWT).

GcpPubsubSourceConfig.description:
GCP Pub/Sub pull source configuration.

**Alpha** (code-complete, not production-validated) and additionally
pending a hyperi-infra issue (TBD). The Pub/Sub pull
source is written but cannot be exercised against the live HyperI GCP
tenant until:

1. A Cloud Logging Log Sink is provisioned to route the desired
   log entries (audit, VPC flow, DNS query, custom workloads) into
   a Pub/Sub topic.
2. A Pub/Sub subscription is created on that topic for the fetcher
   SA to pull from.
3. The fetcher's GCP SA is granted `roles/pubsub.subscriber` on the
   subscription.

Subscriptions are read via the REST `:pull` endpoint (synchronous
pull); the fetcher acknowledges drained messages with `:acknowledge`
after they have been emitted to Kafka. The gRPC StreamingPull variant
is intentionally not used - fetcher volumes do not justify the extra
dependency surface (tonic + protobuf). If a tenant's subscription
ever sustains volumes that REST pull cannot keep up with, revisit
with a v2 source.

Each subscription is one entry under `subscriptions`. The fetcher
emits one record per Pub/Sub message; `message.data` is base64
decoded and parsed as JSON if possible (typical for Log Sink
payloads), otherwise emitted as a string.

service_account_key.description:
Path to a GCP service account JSON key file. The SA must have
`roles/pubsub.subscriber` on every configured subscription.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec for the SA key
(e.g. `vault:secret/gcp-pubsub:sa_key`).

token_url_override.description:
OAuth2 token endpoint override for testing
(default `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`).

subscriptions.description:
Subscriptions to pull from. Each becomes one `FetchResult`
tagged `gcp_pubsub.<subscription-id>`.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

project_id.description: GCP project ID owning the subscription.

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID (the short name, not the fully-qualified path).

max_messages.description: Maximum messages to pull per tick. Default 1000 (the REST API cap).

return_immediately.description:
Whether to return immediately when the subscription is empty,
or block for `returnImmediately=false` server-side wait.
Default true (single-shot, fits the polling fetcher model).

ObjectStoreSourceConfig.description:
Object-store source family configuration.

Polls one or more bucket prefixes across S3 / GCS / Azure Blob,
emitting one record per line of every new object since the cursor.

Only the S3 backend is implemented. GCS and Azure Blob compile but their
`list_new_objects` / `get_object` calls return a not-implemented error, so
configuring one is safe (the source skips it with a warning) and fetches
nothing.

backends.description: One or more cloud-store backends to poll.

topic.description:
Default output topic. Each prefix may override it with its own
`topic:` field.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

ObjectStoreBackendConfig.description:
One backend: provider + auth + buckets/containers to tail.

Provider is selected by the `provider` discriminator (serde-tagged
enum). Each provider variant carries its own auth shape; only S3 is
implemented.

oneOf.description: Amazon S3 (or S3-compatible: MinIO, R2, B2 via endpoint_override).

Google Cloud Storage. **Not implemented** - listing and fetching both
return an error.

Azure Blob Storage. **Not implemented** - listing and fetching both
return an error.

ObjectStoreBucket.description: One bucket / container to tail, plus its prefixes.

bucket.description: Bucket (S3, GCS) or container (Azure Blob) name.

prefixes.description: Prefixes within the bucket to poll. At least one is required.

ObjectStorePrefix.description: One prefix to tail, plus its format and routing.

prefix.description: Object key prefix (may be empty to scan the whole bucket).

format.description: Object format. Drives parser dispatch and gzip handling.

source_tag.description:
Source tag attached to emitted records (e.g. `aws_cloudtrail`,
`aws_vpc_flow`, `gcp_audit_sink`). Becomes the `source` field on
the `FetchResult` as `object_store.<source_tag>`.

topic.description:
Per-prefix Kafka topic override. Falls back to the source-level
`topic` when unset.

ObjectStoreFormat.description: Object body format. Drives gzip handling + parser dispatch.

oneOf.description: Gzipped JSON-lines (one JSON value per newline).
Plain JSON-lines (one JSON value per newline).

Single JSON document (array -> one record per element,
object -> one record).

Gzipped plain text. Emits each non-empty line as `{"line": "..."}` -
there is no ALB / CloudFront / S3 access-log parsing.
Plain text. Same as `text_gz` minus the gunzip step.

region.description: AWS region for SigV4 signing + endpoint construction.

endpoint_override.description:
Optional S3 endpoint override for S3-compatible stores
(MinIO, R2, B2) or for VPC endpoints. When unset, uses
`https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com`.

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID. May be a `vault:` or `env:` spec.

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key. May be a `vault:` or `env:` spec.

credential_secret.description:
Vault secret spec containing both access_key_id +
secret_access_key as a JSON object.
Vault secret spec for the SA key.

account_key.description:
Shared Key (account key). May be a `vault:` or `env:` spec.
Mutually exclusive with `sas_token` and `tenant_id`/`client_*`.

sas_token.description:
SAS token (without leading `?`). Mutually exclusive with
`account_key` and SP credentials.

tenant_id.description: Entra Service-Principal tenant ID (for OAuth2 bearer auth).

client_id.description: Entra Service-Principal client ID (for OAuth2 bearer auth).

client_secret.description: Entra Service-Principal client secret (for OAuth2 bearer auth).

credential_secret.description: Vault secret spec for whichever auth method is in use.

buckets.description:
Blob containers + prefixes to tail. The `bucket` field on each
entry is the container name.

SalesforceSourceConfig.description:
Salesforce audit source configuration.

**Alpha** (code-complete, not production-validated) and additionally
pending a Salesforce connected app + integration user for live testing
(same status as [`GoogleWorkspaceSourceConfig`] and
[`GcpPubsubSourceConfig`]). The fetcher code is complete but cannot be
live-tested until a connected app is provisioned in a HyperI Salesforce org.

Pulls security/audit data from a Salesforce org via the REST API:
- `setup_audit_trail` - admin config changes (SOQL, every org)
- `login_history` - login events (SOQL, every org)
- `event_log_file` - runtime events as downloadable CSV log files
  (7 event types free with 1-day retention; 70+ with the Event
  Monitoring / Shield add-on)

Auth is OAuth2 against `<login_url>/services/oauth2/token`, via one of
two server-to-server flows selected by which fields are set:
- **JWT bearer** (Salesforce-recommended): set `client_id` (connected
  app consumer key), `username` (integration user), and one of
  `private_key` / `private_key_secret` (RSA private key PEM). An RS256
  JWT is signed and exchanged for a token.
- **client credentials**: set `client_id` + one of `client_secret` /
  `credential_secret`. Requires the connected app to have the client-
  credentials flow enabled with a run-as user.

The token response carries an `instance_url` which is used for all
subsequent API calls (not `login_url`). `instance_url_override` pins it
for testing or custom-domain deployments.

login_url.description:
OAuth2 login base URL. Default `https://login.salesforce.com`.
Sandboxes use `https://test.salesforce.com`; My Domain orgs may use
`https://<mydomain>.my.salesforce.com`.

api_version.description: REST API version path segment. Default `v60.0`.

client_id.description:
Connected app consumer key. Used as the JWT `iss` claim (JWT bearer)
or the `client_id` form field (client credentials).

username.description: Integration username (JWT `sub` claim). JWT-bearer flow only.

private_key.description:
RSA private key PEM for the JWT-bearer flow (full
`-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` ... block). JWT-bearer flow only.

private_key_secret.description:
Secret source spec resolving to the RSA private key PEM
(e.g. `vault:secret/salesforce:private_key`). Takes precedence over
`private_key` when set. JWT-bearer flow only.

client_secret.description: Connected app consumer secret. client-credentials flow only.

credential_secret.description:
Secret source spec resolving to the consumer secret
(e.g. `vault:secret/salesforce:client_secret`). Takes precedence
over `client_secret` when set. client-credentials flow only.

instance_url_override.description:
Pin the API instance URL instead of using the token response's
`instance_url`. For testing or custom-domain deployments.

filter.description: CEL filter expression applied to fetched records.

connections.description:
Multiple Salesforce orgs of this type, each polled independently.
Empty = a single implicit connection from the fields above.

SalesforceService.description:
Salesforce service. `name` selects the audit surface:
`setup_audit_trail`, `login_history`, or `event_log_file`.

config.description:
Service-specific configuration. Recognised keys (event_log_file):
- `event_types`: array of EventType values to include (default all)
- `interval`: `"Hourly"` or `"Daily"` (default `"Daily"`)

SalesforceConnection.description:
One Salesforce connection: an org + its OAuth2 credentials (JWT-bearer or
client-credentials). Type-wide fields (`services`, `topic`, `filter`) are
shared and stay on [`SalesforceSourceConfig`].

id.description: Stable, unique connection id (cursor key + metric/log label).

username.description: Integration username (JWT `sub` claim). JWT-bearer flow only.

private_key.description: RSA private key PEM for the JWT-bearer flow.

private_key_secret.description: Secret source spec resolving to the RSA private key PEM.

client_secret.description: Connected app consumer secret (client-credentials flow only).

credential_secret.description: Secret source spec resolving to the consumer secret ("provider:path:key").

instance_url_override.description: Pin the API instance URL for this connection.

plugins.description: Deprecated plugin config (kept for backwards-compatible deserialisation).

ContainerExtractorConfig.description:
Container-based extractor configuration.

Each container runs an isolated extraction tool (any language/runtime).
One container per source + config — no horizontal scaling needed.

name.description: Unique name for this extractor instance.

topic.description: Output Kafka topic for this extractor's data.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the container.

timeout_secs.description: Timeout in seconds for scheduled (one-shot) containers (0 = no timeout).

max_restart_attempts.description: Maximum restart attempts for continuous mode (0 = unlimited).

max_restart_backoff_secs.description: Maximum backoff delay between restarts in seconds.

stable_after_secs.description: Seconds of stable running before resetting backoff counter.

PluginsConfig.description: Deprecated plugin configuration — logs warning if non-empty values present.

grpc_bind_address.description: gRPC bind address for receiving Vector sink data.

IngestConfig.description:
HTTP ingest server for container extractors to post data.

Off unless a deployment enables it. `/ingest/{source}/{topic}` takes the
destination topic from the URL, so an exposed listener with no token lets
anything that can reach the port write to any topic.

enabled.description: Enable ingest HTTP endpoint. Off by default.

max_body_size.description: Maximum request body size in bytes.

auth_token.description:
Bearer token for authentication (credential resolver format).
Empty or absent = no auth (backward compatible, logs warning).

KafkaConfig.description:
Legacy Kafka producer configuration.

**Deprecated:** Use `output.kafka` (scalo `KafkaConfig`) instead.
This struct is kept for backward compatibility with existing config files
that use the top-level `kafka:` section. Will be removed in next major version.

Migration: move your `kafka:` settings under `output.kafka:` using scalo
`KafkaConfig` format (profiles, `librdkafka_overrides`, standard field names).

topic_suffix.description: Suffix appended to source topic names.

SaslConfig.description:
SASL authentication configuration.

Every field defaults, so the two secret env vars the chart injects are a
complete SASL block on their own -- which is what the chart claims they are.
Without that, a partial block was a startup parse error.

enabled.description:
Enable SASL. Defaults to TRUE, because reaching this struct at all means
a `kafka.sasl` block exists -- written by hand or built out of the two
secret env vars the chart injects -- and that is a request for SASL.
`enabled: false` still switches it off and is never inferred away.
`kafka.sasl` itself defaults to absent, so a config that says nothing
gets no SASL.

mechanism.description:
SASL mechanism, in librdkafka's spelling: `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`,
`SCRAM-SHA-512`, `GSSAPI`, `OAUTHBEARER`. Passed through verbatim, so
anything else is refused by the client at connect.

password.description:
Password (always redacted in serialisation/debug output).

The schema default is pinned to the empty string: serialising the real
default outside an expose window yields the mask, and a UI that
pre-filled a password box with `***REDACTED***` would send that as the
password.

compression.description: Compression type (none, gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd).

memory_limit.description: Maximum memory for buffers in bytes (0 = auto-detect 67% of available).

queue_capacity.description:
Bounded mpsc capacity. When the queue is full, `try_send` returns
`QueueFull` (overflow=Drop). Sized for failure-burst tolerance.
Default 10_000.

batch_size.description:
Drain coalesces up to this many entries into one backend write.
Default 256.

flush_interval_ms.description:
Flush a partial batch after this duration, even if not full.
Default 100 ms.

DlqMode.description: How backends are used when multiple are enabled.

oneOf.description:
Try backends in order; stop on first success.
Default order: Kafka first, file fallback.
Write to all enabled backends; report any failures.
File backend only (no Kafka dependency).
Kafka backend only (current dfe-loader behaviour).

FileDlqConfig.description:
File-based DLQ configuration.

Writes NDJSON files with automatic rotation and cleanup.

path.description:
Base directory for DLQ files.
Service name is appended as a subdirectory.

max_age_days.description: Auto-cleanup files older than this many days.

oneOf.description: Rotate files every hour.
Rotate files every day.

topic_suffix.description: Suffix appended to destination for per-table routing.

common_topic.description: Common topic when routing is `Common` or destination is unknown.

oneOf.description:
Route to topic matching destination with suffix.
e.g. "acme.auth" → "acme.auth.dlq"
Route all failures to a single common topic.

grpc.description: gRPC transport configuration (scalo GrpcConfig, client mode).

topic_suffix.description:
Suffix appended to source topic names (e.g., "_land").
If set, takes precedence over legacy `kafka.topic_suffix`.

destinations.description:
Named destinations beyond the default transports, keyed by name.

The default destination is the source's own -- its topic on the bus,
the configured endpoint on the direct transport. A destination declared
here is reached by a [`route`](Self::routes) naming it, so a record can
go to a transform instead of, or as well as, the default.

routes.description: Per-record routes over the named destinations (first match wins).

KafkaConfig2.description:
Kafka transport configuration.

Uses a profile-based system where profiles provide opinionated defaults,
and `librdkafka_overrides` allows overriding any setting.

profile.description:
Configuration profile (production, devtest).

The profile provides baseline librdkafka settings optimized for the use case.
Use `librdkafka_overrides` to customize specific settings.

client_id.description: Client ID for identification in broker logs.

group_instance_id.description:
Static group membership id (`group.instance.id`). Opt-in: `None` (the
default) uses dynamic membership.

Set this to a STABLE, UNIQUE-per-replica value (the K8s pod name is the
canonical choice -- e.g. from `$HOSTNAME` / the downward API) to take
static membership (KIP-345). A static member that restarts rejoins with
its prior partitions WITHOUT triggering a group-wide rebalance, which
turns a rolling restart of a large consumer fleet from dozens of
stop-the-world rebalances into zero. Two replicas sharing one value get
fenced -- the value MUST be unique per replica.

auto_discover.description:
Enable auto-discovery when `topics` is empty.
When false (default), empty `topics` means no subscription (producer-only).
When true, empty `topics` triggers broker auto-discovery with
`topic_include`/`topic_exclude` filters and suppression rules.

topic_include.description:
Regex patterns for topic include filtering (empty = accept all).
Topics must match at least one pattern (OR logic).

topic_exclude.description:
Regex patterns for topic exclude filtering.
Topics matching any pattern are excluded. Exclude wins over include.
Default: `["^__", "_dlq$"]` -- Kafka internal topics and the DFE
standard's dead-letter topics (a DLQ consumer sets its own include).

topic_refresh_secs.description:
Periodic topic refresh interval in seconds (0 = disabled).
Only applies when `topics` is empty (auto-discovery mode).

topic_suppression_rules.description:
Suppression rules: if a topic with preferred_suffix exists,
suppress the topic with suppressed_suffix for the same base name.
Default: _load suppresses _land (the convention).

provider.description:
Optional managed-Kafka provider name (strimzi / redpanda / confluent-cloud /
redpanda-cloud / msk / plaintext). When set, DERIVES security_protocol +
sasl_mechanism from the opt-in provider presets -- the caller does NOT
hand-set them. Applied by [`apply_provider`](KafkaConfig::apply_provider)
before validate(). See [`providers`](super::providers).

ssl_ca_location.description:
SSL CA certificate file path (private-CA bundle; maps to
`TlsTrust.extra_roots` -- a single combined root+intermediate PEM is
accepted).

ssl_skip_verify.description:
Skip SSL certificate verification.

Automatically enabled for `devtest` profile.

allow_insecure_transport.description:
Deliberately permit an unencrypted transport (`plaintext` /
`sasl_plaintext`) in production. Default `false`: production
[`validate`](KafkaConfig::validate) rejects unencrypted transports so a
misconfiguration cannot ship data/credentials in the clear. Set `true`
only for an audited case (e.g. mesh-encrypted in-cluster traffic).

enable_auto_commit.description: Enable auto-commit (default: false for manual commit).

max_partition_fetch_bytes.description: Maximum messages per partition per poll.

sizing.description:
Kafka sizing surface: profile + named knobs + raw librdkafka escape hatch.

Controls the byte-budget and latency envelope for GET (consumer) and
SEND (producer) paths. See [`KafkaSizingConfig`] for full documentation.

Example YAML:
```yaml
kafka:
  sizing:
    profile: throughput
    consumer:
      fetch_min_bytes: 2097152  # 2 MiB, overrides profile default
    producer:
      compression_type: zstd    # opt into zstd for storage-bound topics
    consumer_librdkafka:
      fetch.wait.max.ms: "75"   # raw override wins over everything
    producer_librdkafka:
      linger.ms: "50"
```

librdkafka_overrides.description:
Librdkafka configuration overrides.

These settings override both the profile defaults and explicit config fields.
Use this to customize any librdkafka setting not exposed as an explicit field.

Example:
```yaml
librdkafka_overrides:
  statistics.interval.ms: "5000"
  fetch.min.bytes: "2097152"
```

filters_in.description: Inbound message filters (applied on recv before caller sees messages).

filters_out.description: Outbound message filters (applied on send before transport dispatches).

KafkaProfile.description:
Kafka configuration profile.

Profiles provide opinionated librdkafka defaults for specific use cases.
Users can override any setting via `librdkafka_overrides`.

oneOf.description:
Production profile: lean baseline for all data-plane services.

Only sets values that differ from librdkafka defaults.
Services add overrides via `librdkafka_overrides`.

Development/test profile: fast iteration, low memory.

Cooperative rebalancing, fast reconnects, debug logging.
SSL certificate verification disabled by default.

SuppressionRule.description:
Topic suppression rule for auto-discovery.

When auto-discovering topics, if a topic with `preferred_suffix` exists
for a base name, the topic with `suppressed_suffix` for that same base
is removed. Default: `_load` suppresses `_land`.

preferred_suffix.description: The suffix of the preferred (kept) topic.

suppressed_suffix.description: The suffix of the suppressed (removed) topic.

KafkaSizingConfig.description:
Kafka sizing surface: profile + named per-knob overrides + raw escape hatch.

Resolution precedence (lowest to highest):
1. `SelfRegulationProfile` defaults
2. Named knobs in `consumer` / `producer` (explicit `Some(v)` wins)
3. Raw librdkafka maps `consumer_librdkafka` / `producer_librdkafka` (wins
   over everything, applied last via `ClientConfig::set`)

The raw maps are logged (one line per key) when they override a property
that the sizing surface depends on (the fetch byte sizes and
`enable.auto.commit`).

consumer.description: Per-knob consumer overrides (any `Some(v)` beats the profile default).

producer.description: Per-knob producer overrides (any `Some(v)` beats the profile default).

consumer_librdkafka.description:
Raw librdkafka consumer properties applied LAST, winning over everything.

Keys must be valid librdkafka property names (e.g. `fetch.wait.max.ms`).
An invalid key silently no-ops in librdkafka -- double-check spelling.

producer_librdkafka.description:
Raw librdkafka producer properties applied LAST, winning over everything.

Keys must be valid librdkafka property names (e.g. `linger.ms`).

SelfRegulationProfile.description:
Opinionated sizing profile for the Kafka GET/SEND surface.

The profile sets default values for all named knobs below. An explicit
per-knob value in [`KafkaSizingConfig`] always wins over the profile
default. The raw librdkafka escape hatch in [`KafkaConfig`] wins over
everything.

Profiles target the BYTE-level throughput budget and latency envelope:

| Profile | Use case |
|---|---|
| `throughput` (default) | PB/day batch ingest, large fanout topics |
| `balanced` | Mixed OLTP + analytics, moderate batch size |
| `low_latency` | Near-real-time, event-driven, small messages |

oneOf.description:
Maximum throughput: generous byte budgets, tolerates batching delay.

Consumer: 1 MiB fetch.min.bytes, 50 ms wait, 10 MiB per-partition,
100 MiB total, 2000 poll-safety cap.
Producer: 128 KiB batch, 20 ms linger, lz4, 64 MiB buffer, 5 in-flight.

Balanced: moderate batching, 5 ms linger, smaller per-partition budget.

Consumer: 256 KiB fetch.min.bytes, 25 ms wait, 5 MiB per-partition,
50 MiB total, 1000 poll-safety cap.
Producer: 64 KiB batch, 5 ms linger, lz4, 32 MiB buffer, 5 in-flight.

Low latency: minimal batching delay, smaller buffers.

Consumer: 1 byte fetch.min.bytes, 5 ms wait, 1 MiB per-partition,
10 MiB total, 500 poll-safety cap.
Producer: 16 KiB batch, 0 ms linger, lz4, 16 MiB buffer, 5 in-flight.

ConsumerKnobs.description:
Named consumer sizing knobs.

All fields are `Option<T>`: `None` means "use the profile default".
An explicit `Some(v)` wins over the profile default.

fetch_min_bytes.description:
Minimum bytes the broker must have ready before responding to a Fetch.

librdkafka: `fetch.min.bytes` (default 1 byte).
Raising this batches more data per round-trip but adds latency when
topic traffic is low.

fetch_max_wait_ms.description:
Maximum milliseconds the broker may wait to fill `fetch.min.bytes`.

librdkafka: `fetch.wait.max.ms` (default 500 ms).
Works in tandem with `fetch_min_bytes` -- the broker returns whatever
it has when this timer fires even if `fetch.min.bytes` is not met.

max_partition_fetch_bytes.description:
Maximum bytes returned per partition per Fetch request.

librdkafka: `max.partition.fetch.bytes` (alias `fetch.message.max.bytes`,
default 1 MiB). Must be >= the topic's `max.message.bytes`.

fetch_max_bytes.description:
Maximum total bytes returned by the broker for a single Fetch request
across all partitions.

librdkafka: `fetch.max.bytes` (default 50 MiB).

max_poll_records.description:
Maximum number of messages the recv() loop returns per call.

NOTE: `max.poll.records` does NOT exist in librdkafka -- there is no
broker-level property for this. This is a purely CLIENT-SIDE cap,
enforced by passing this value as the `max` argument to
`KafkaTransport::recv()` via `KafkaSizingConfig::effective_poll_cap()`.
It bounds the batch size delivered to the WorkBatch layer, not the
network fetch size (which is byte-governed by the knobs above).

ProducerKnobs.description:
Named producer sizing knobs.

All fields are `Option<T>`: `None` means "use the profile default".

batch_size_bytes.description:
Maximum bytes per MessageSet (librdkafka `batch.size`, default 1 MiB).

This is the PER-BATCH ceiling, not the total queue size. Raise this for
fewer, larger network writes. Note: `batch.size` in librdkafka is in
bytes (matches the Java Kafka client name and unit).

linger_ms.description:
Accumulation delay before transmitting a MessageSet.

librdkafka: `linger.ms` (alias for `queue.buffering.max.ms`, default 5 ms).
Higher values fill larger batches; 0 sends immediately.

compression_type.description:
Compression codec for MessageSets.

librdkafka: `compression.type` (alias for `compression.codec`).
Valid values: `none`, `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, `zstd`.
Default (all profiles): `lz4` -- best throughput/ratio tradeoff.
Use `zstd` for storage-bound topics that can absorb the CPU cost.

buffer_memory_bytes.description:
Total byte budget for the producer's in-memory queue.

librdkafka: `queue.buffering.max.kbytes` (in KiB, default 1 GiB).
This is the TOTAL queue, not per-batch. Set lower to bound memory
usage in containers. Stored as bytes in this struct; divided by 1024
when applied to librdkafka.

max_in_flight.description:
Maximum concurrent in-flight requests per broker connection.

librdkafka: `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection` (default 1,000,000).
Set to 5 to match the exactly-once safe limit (KIP-98) and to bound
memory/reorder window. Matches the Java Kafka producer default for
idempotent producers.

idempotence.description:
Enable the Kafka idempotent producer (`enable.idempotence`).

`None` (default) -> ON: scalo enables idempotence by default (v2.10) as
the cheap "effectively-once" step -- it dedups producer-retry writes in
the broker at near-zero cost. Idempotence REQUIRES `acks=all`,
`max.in.flight<=5` and `retries>0`, so when on
[`resolved_producer_map`](KafkaSizingConfig::resolved_producer_map)
forces `acks=all` and clamps `max.in.flight` to 5. Set `Some(false)` to
opt out (e.g. a latency-bound topic that wants `acks=1`). The raw
`producer_librdkafka` escape hatch still wins over this.

FilterRule.description:
A single filter rule -- CEL expression + disposition action.

Written in CEL syntax regardless of execution tier. The engine determines
the optimal execution strategy at construction time.

# Examples

```yaml
- expression: 'has(_table)'
  action: drop
- expression: 'status == "poison"'
  action: dlq
```

expression.description: CEL expression to evaluate against each message payload.

action.description: Action to take when the expression matches. Defaults to `drop`.

FilterAction.description: Disposition action when a filter matches.

oneOf.description: Silently discard the message (counted in metrics).
Route the message to the dead-letter queue (counted + security audit).

GrpcConfig.description:
gRPC transport configuration.

Supports client mode (sending), server mode (receiving), or both.

# Client mode

Set `endpoint` to connect to a remote gRPC server.

# Server mode

Set `listen` to accept incoming Push RPCs.

# Both

Set both for bidirectional communication (e.g., a relay node).

listen.description:
Server listen address (e.g., "0.0.0.0:6000").
When set, the transport accepts incoming Push RPCs.

endpoint.description:
Client endpoint URI (e.g., "http://loader:6000").
When set, the transport can send messages to a remote server.

recv_buffer_size.description: Receive buffer size (messages buffered from incoming RPCs).

send_timeout_ms.description:
Per-RPC send deadline in milliseconds (0 = no deadline).

Bounds a single `push` so a hung/black-holing server cannot block a
sender task forever. Applied as the `grpc-timeout` header. Default 30s.

max_message_size.description: Maximum message size in bytes (both send and receive).

compression.description: Enable gzip compression for gRPC messages.

tls_enabled.description: Enable client TLS for the `endpoint` connection.

tls_ca_path.description:
Private-CA PEM (maps to `TlsTrust.extra_roots`). When unset with
`tls_enabled`, falls back to OS native roots.

tls_domain.description: Domain name for SNI / certificate verification (overrides the URI host).

vector_compat.description:
Enable Vector wire protocol compatibility on the same server.
When true, the server also accepts `/vector.Vector/PushEvents` RPCs
from legacy Vector sinks.
Requires the `transport-grpc-vector-compat` feature.

filters_in.description: Inbound message filters (applied on recv before caller sees messages).

filters_out.description: Outbound message filters (applied on send before transport dispatches).

DestinationSpec.description: A declared destination: exactly one transport block.

grpc.description:
Deliver over gRPC to a scalo Push listener (a transform, the loader,
the archiver).

config.description: Broker settings for this destination. Unset reuses the output's own.

topic.description: Fixed topic. Unset means the record's own source topic.

OutputRoute.description:
A per-record route: matched records go to the named destination(s) instead
of the default.

destination.description: Destination for matched records: one name, or a list to fan out.

DestinationRef.description:
One destination name, or a list of them to fan a matched record out to.

A fan-out is delivered when every destination has accepted it.

anyOf.description: Several destination names -- the record goes to all of them.

CursorConfig.description:
Cursor store configuration for incremental fetching.

Cursors are stored as individual JSON files in `directory`, one per
source service (e.g., `aws.cloudtrail.cursor.json`). The directory
should be PVC-backed for pod restart persistence.

If `directory` is empty, the cursor store falls back to the config
file's parent directory with a warning.

directory.description:
Directory for cursor files. Each source gets its own file
named `{instance_id}.{source}.{service}.cursor.json`.
Empty = fall back to config file directory (with warning).

default_window_hours.description: Default lookback window in hours when no cursor exists.

ScalingPressureConfig.description:
Base configuration for scaling pressure calculation.

Lives in the app's config cascade so thresholds are env-var overridable
(e.g., `DFE_LOADER__SCALING__MEMORY_GATE_THRESHOLD=0.9`).

Component weights and saturation points are app-specific -- defined in
each app's config and passed to [`super::ScalingPressure::new`] via
[`ScalingComponent`].

enabled.description:
Enable scaling pressure calculation.
When disabled, `calculate()` always returns 0.0.

memory_gate_threshold.description:
Memory usage ratio that triggers the memory gate (0.0-1.0).

When `memory_used / memory_limit >= threshold`, scaling pressure
is forced to 100.0 to trigger immediate scale-up before OOM.
